clips.text: The last train arrives without a sound. Every carriage is empty, except for a woman holding a yellow umbrella. Your phone lights up. A message from your own number: whatever you do, do not miss this train. The doors begin to close.

The woman smiles. You are late, she says. Outside, the city runs backwards: rain rises into clouds, a fallen cup becomes whole. She offers you the umbrella. At the far end of the carriage, the driver is calling your name.

The train leaves. Your phone rings from inside the station intercom. Your own voice whispers: I waited too. Then the departure board changes. One train remaining. Destination: the day you wish you could change. A service door clicks open.

Years ago, you lent this umbrella to a stranger in the rain. You never got it back. I was on my way to say goodbye, she says. Your kindness gave me the courage to go. Tonight, I can take you back to one moment. Or I can take you home.

There is no driver. Only a microphone, a yellow umbrella, and a recording of your voice. You sent the warning. You brought yourself here. A switch has two positions: send the message again, or let the next morning arrive.

You climb the stairs into morning. A cleaner waves. The city smells of coffee and wet pavement. Your phone holds one new message: good choice. You delete it, buy two coffees, and give one away. Some mysteries are invitations to keep living.

You stand at the old bus stop. Your younger self offers a yellow umbrella to a crying stranger. She catches her bus. Through its window, someone reaches for her hand. You cannot change the past. But now you know: you made a difference. You always did.

You close your eyes. When you open them, sunlight fills an ordinary train. A yellow umbrella rests beside you. Your phone is quiet. At your stop, someone is waiting in the rain. This time, you know exactly what to do.

You press record. Whatever you do, do not miss this train. The room dissolves into platform lights. Somewhere, your phone lights up. The last train arrives without a sound. This time, you are the one holding the yellow umbrella.
